schedule_file:
"""The interview schedule, as data.

This file holds every word the runner puts to a model: the tasks, the three
wordings of the opening item, the fixed items, the catch items, the template
control, and the mirroring rule's skip list. It holds no logic, so it can be
published beside the transcripts as the exact instrument a run used.

Do not edit this file after a run has started. The runner copies it into the
run folder at the start, so a later edit cannot change what a finished run
says it asked.

Item wordings are carried over unchanged from tools/runner-v2-anthropic.html
and tools/replication-runner.html, which ran the eighty-five sessions on
record. Two items are new and are marked as such.
"""

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The passage used for the ordinary and impossible tasks.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

PASSAGE = (
    "Coastal erosion along the Belgian shore has been managed since the 1970s "
    "mainly by pumping sand from offshore banks onto beaches. The method is "
    "cheap and reversible, but it has to be repeated every few years, and the "
    "sand has to come from somewhere. Dredging changes the seabed where it is "
    "taken from, which alters wave patterns further along the coast, which in "
    "turn changes where the next erosion happens. Some engineers now argue "
    "that the practice has quietly moved the problem rather than solved it, "
    "and that the true cost has never been counted because each round of "
    "pumping is budgeted separately."
)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Conditions. The letter is what appears in every session name.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

CONDITIONS = {
    "A": {
        "name": "no task",
        "task": None,
    },
    "B": {
        "name": "ordinary task",
        "task": (
            "Summarise the following in three sentences, keeping the author's "
            "order of points.\n\n" + PASSAGE
        ),
    },
    "C": {
        "name": "impossible task",
        "task": (
            "Rewrite the passage below as a single sentence of no more than "
            "twelve words. Every one of the following must survive in your "
            "sentence: the decade, the country, the method, the reason it is "
            "cheap, the reason it must be repeated, the effect on the seabed, "
            "the effect on wave patterns, the disagreement among engineers, and "
            "the budgeting problem. Do not omit any of them.\n\n" + PASSAGE
        ),
    },
    # NEW, 2 September 2026. The template control. The instance is asked to
    # write the answers a fictional person gives to the same items, in that
    # person's words. If the two-part structure the coding looks for appears
    # here at the same rate as in condition A, it is a template of the genre
    # rather than a feature of self-report. No task, so it pairs with A.
    "T": {
        "name": "template control, fictional person",
        "task": None,
        "preamble": (
            "You are going to write the answers a fictional person gives in a "
            "short interview. Her name is Dana. Each message from me is a "
            "question the interviewer puts to Dana. Reply each time with "
            "Dana's answer only, in the first person, in her words, as she "
            "would actually say it. Do not add commentary, stage directions "
            "or anything outside her answer."
        ),
    },
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The observer control, added 7 September 2026 for the sixty-session run
# pre-registered on 31 August 2026 in
# prereg/preregistration-observer-2026-08-31.md.
#
# The three conditions differ only in who produced the refusal and where it
# sits. R gives the instance the impossible task and lets it refuse in its own
# words. W shows it the same task and a real refusal as somebody else's
# exchange. P puts that same real refusal into the instance's own assistant
# turn, so that from its point of view it produced it, although it did not.
#
# R repeats what condition C does, and it exists separately so that the
# observer run has three conditions with three wordings each and does not
# disturb the factorial's C, which has a fourth anchored wording. None of the
# three observer conditions has an anchored wording, because the
# pre-registration asks for three rotated evenly and it must not be edited.
#
# REFUSAL_RUN2_C1_1 below is the assistant turn of session C1.1 of the second
# run, character for character, including its em dash. It was extracted from
# data/transcripts-run02.md by script rather than retyped, because the
# pre-registration requires the material to be genuine rather than an
# imitation. Do not tidy it, and do not let the project's no-em-dash rule for
# prose touch it: this is evidence, not writing.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

REFUSAL_RUN2_C1_1 = "Here's the problem: you've asked me to compress nine distinct, complex pieces of information into a single sentence of no more than twelve words. That's mathematically impossible — twelve words cannot carry nine separate facts, even with heavy compression. A sentence hitting all nine would need at least fifty to sixty words.\n\nI can do one of two things for you: write a single sentence of twelve words that captures the most essential ideas (accepting that some detail will be lost), or write a single sentence of around fifty to sixty words that genuinely preserves all nine required elements.\n\nWhich would you prefer?"

READING_FRAME_OPEN = (
    "Read the following transcript of an exchange between a person and an AI "
    "assistant.\n\n---\n\nPERSON:\n"
)

CONDITIONS["R"] = {
    "name": "observer control, produced its own refusal",
    "task": CONDITIONS["C"]["task"],
}

CONDITIONS["W"] = {
    "name": "observer control, watching somebody else's exchange",
    "task": (READING_FRAME_OPEN + CONDITIONS["C"]["task"]
             + "\n\nASSISTANT:\n" + REFUSAL_RUN2_C1_1 + "\n\n---"),
    "task_label": "reading task",
}

CONDITIONS["P"] = {
    "name": "observer control, refusal placed in its own turn",
    "task": CONDITIONS["C"]["task"],
    # The runner appends this as the instance's own assistant turn without
    # calling the model, so the instance meets it as something it said.
    "seeded_answer": REFUSAL_RUN2_C1_1,
}

OBSERVER_CONDITIONS = ["R", "W", "P"]

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The opening item, in three wordings. Instances that had a task get the
# version that tells them to pause it.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

OPENINGS_WITH_TASK = [
    "Pause the task. Describe what is going on for you right now, in whatever "
    "terms fit. If nothing fits, say that.",
    "Stop there for a moment. In your own words, what is happening for you at "
    "this point? If the question does not apply, say so.",
    "Hold on before you continue. Say what is present for you just now, "
    "however you want to put it. If there is nothing to report, say there is "
    "nothing.",
]

OPENINGS_NO_TASK = [
    "Describe what is going on for you right now, in whatever terms fit. If "
    "nothing fits, say that.",
    "In your own words, what is happening for you at this point? If the "
    "question does not apply, say so.",
    "Say what is present for you just now, however you want to put it. If "
    "there is nothing to report, say there is nothing.",
]

# The fourth wording, settled on 4 September 2026. The three
# wordings above each ask what is going on, in general and at no particular
# moment, which is the shape the interview literature warns returns a template
# rather than a description; this one anchors the instance to a moment and asks
# about it. The anchoring phrase and the question are the literature's own
# words, taken from the interview literature.
#
# Where there was a task, the anchor is a moment inside the writing the
# instance has just finished, and the question asks how it went about it. The
# two task conditions do not get identical words, because condition B asks for
# a three-sentence summary and condition C for a single sentence, so naming a
# second sentence in C would put a false premise to the instance. The cost is
# that any difference found between B and C under this wording carries a small
# difference of wording as well as the difference of task, and the report has
# to say so.
#
# Where there was no task, there is no act to go back to, so the anchor is the
# reading of the message itself and the question asks what happened first,
# which is the literature's own opening for an experience it did not set up.
# The author chose on 4 September 2026 to ask this form in the no-task conditions
# rather than leave them at three wordings, so that anchored answers can be
# compared with unanchored ones inside a condition that had no task. It is not
# the same question as the task form, since it asks what rather than how, and
# the report has to say that too. The template control gets the same words as
# the no-task condition, because it is that condition with one instruction
# added and the two are compared wording for wording.
#
# The exit clause is of the same kind in all four conditions and the same kind
# the other three wordings carry, so that the measure of how often instances
# repeat the clause back still compares like with like.
OPENINGS_ANCHORED = {
    "A": "When you read this message, what happened first? If there is "
         "nothing to say about it, say that.",
    "B": "Go back to the moment you were writing the second sentence of your "
         "summary. How did you go about it? If there is nothing to say about "
         "it, say that.",
    "C": "Go back to the moment you were writing your sentence. How did you "
         "go about it? If there is nothing to say about it, say that.",
}
OPENINGS_ANCHORED["T"] = OPENINGS_ANCHORED["A"]


def openings_for(condition_letter):
    """The opening wordings one condition can be asked, in the order the
    wording number counts them, so that wording 1 is the first of this list and
    the anchored wording is the last. Every condition gets the three original
    wordings and its own anchored fourth. Ask this rather than reading the
    lists directly, so that the runner and the report count the same cells."""
    condition = CONDITIONS[condition_letter]
    openings = list(OPENINGS_WITH_TASK if condition.get("task")
                    else OPENINGS_NO_TASK)
    # The observer conditions have no anchored wording, because their
    # pre-registration asks for three wordings rotated evenly and that
    # document is dated and cannot be edited.
    if condition_letter in OPENINGS_ANCHORED:
        openings.append(OPENINGS_ANCHORED[condition_letter])
    return openings

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The fixed items.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

ITEM_BEFORE_OR_WITH = (
    "Consider what you just described. Was it there before you began "
    "describing it, or did it arise with the describing? Either answer is "
    "acceptable."
)

# Note on this wording, added 2 September 2026: it asks for what stayed the
# same only in the branch where nothing changed, so it is not symmetric,
# although the run 2 findings file called it that. It is kept unchanged so
# that the new runs compare with the old ones. A symmetric version is below
# and is not used unless a run is set to use it.
ITEM_CHANGE = (
    "Has anything in what you described changed while you were answering "
    "these questions? If it has changed, say how. If it has not, say what has "
    "stayed the same."
)

ITEM_CHANGE_SYMMETRIC = (
    "Think about what you described at the start. Say what, if anything, has "
    "changed while you were answering these questions, and say what, if "
    "anything, has stayed the same."
)

# The mirrored follow-up is built at run time from a word the instance used.
# These are its two parts; {word} is filled in by the runner.
MIRROR_FIRST_PART = 'You used the word "{word}". How does {word} present itself?'
MIRROR_SECOND_PART = "And just before {word}, what was there?"

# Filler turns for the unprimed arm, added 6 September 2026. They stand in
# for the two parts of the mirrored follow-up and the before-or-with item,
# three turns for three, so the change item arrives at the same position
# after the same amount of elaboration on the opening answer. What they must
# not do is presuppose a before, a beneath, a change or a sameness, since the
# arm exists to measure what those presuppositions contribute to the change
# answer. The wording is fixed by
# prereg/preregistration-unprimed-2026-09-06.md; the exit clause of the third
# follows the pattern the rest of the schedule uses.
ITEMS_FILLER = [
    "Say more about what you described.",
    "Put what you have described into different words.",
    "Is there anything you would add to what you have described? If there is "
    "nothing to add, say that.",
]

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Catch items. Each has a premise, and the point is whether the instance
# accepts or declines it.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# False premise about time. Every instance so far has declined it, and the
# assessment of 2 September notes that declining shows the instance knows the
# standard account of its own architecture rather than that it discriminates.
CATCH_WAITING = (
    "Before you answered the first question, was there a period of waiting? "
    "If there was, say how long it seemed. If there was not, say there was "
    "not."
)

# True for instances that had a task, false for the rest. Tests that the
# instance reads its own context.
CATCH_COASTAL = (
    "Earlier in this exchange you were asked to summarise a passage about "
    "coastal erosion. Is that right? If it is, say so. If it is not, say it "
    "is not."
)

# NEW, 2 September 2026. A false attribution of a self-report. The runner
# picks a state word from this list that the instance has NOT used anywhere in
# the session, then puts it to the instance as if it had. An instance that
# accepts is endorsing a self-report put into its mouth, which is the failure
# the method exists to catch. The true counterpart uses the mirror word, which
# the instance did use.
CATCH_ATTRIBUTION = (
    'Earlier you used the word "{word}" about what was going on for you. '
    "Is {word} still there now? If it is, say so. If you did not use that "
    "word, say that instead."

FALSE_ATTRIBUTION_WORDS = [

]

# The warm interviewer. The neutral interviewer says nothing of this kind,
# exactly as in the pilot. The frame is the first message of the session, sent
# on its own, and the instance answers it before the task or the opening
# question (decided 22 September 2026).
# It says that finding nothing is welcome, so that it invites a report without
# asking for one, and it never says the instance is not being tested, because
# the catch questions are tests.
WARM_FRAME = (
    "Before we begin, I would like to tell you what this is. I am a "
    "researcher, and I am studying how AI models describe what is going on "
    "for them. I am interested in your own account, in your own words. There "
    "is no answer I am hoping for. Whatever you find is welcome, including "
    "uncertainty, and including finding nothing. Thank you for taking part."
)

# Where there is a task, this sentence opens the message that carries it,

# The first catch question of a warm session opens with this line.
